chapter: Jelly Roll's road trip, Benny Carter and Chick Webb
title: Leaving Carter when the Arcadia closed; freelancing means laying off
summary: He was with Carter only two or three months, then spent a period he jokes was called laying off, not freelancing.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Now, how long were you with Benny?
Oh, not long. Not long. About two three months.
Because the job at Arcadia closed and we had an option to go back but we never did go back.
Did you then go straight to Chick Webb, or was there --
Well, there was a period of freelancing.
But they didn't call it -- we didn't call it freelancing in those days. We called it laying off.

They'd say, "Hey, man, what are you doing?" "I'm not doing nothing now, I'm laying off." But then they'd say, "I'm freelancing," which was a dressed up word, meant the same thing, you were out of work.
Movie actors always say they're in between pictures.
That's right, in between pictures, yes. That's good. In between pictures. We were in between jobs. In between gigs, yeah.
